explain.say: Every box on the periodic table hides a little code. Once you can read it, you can count what is inside any atom! Look at the board. Let us take sodium, the metal in your table salt.

explain.say: See the smaller number, 11? That is the atomic number. It tells you how many protons are in the nucleus. Every sodium atom has exactly 11. How many protons would an atom with atomic number 6 have?

explain.say: Six! Here is a bonus for you. An atom has no overall charge, so its electrons match its protons. Look at the third step: sodium has 11 electrons too. Easy, right? How many electrons does oxygen, atomic number 8, have?

faq.a: The atomic number is the number of protons in an atom. It is also called the proton number, and it decides which element the atom is.
asks: What does the atomic number tell you?

faq.a: The mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Electrons are left out because they weigh so little.
asks: What does the mass number tell you?

faq.q: How do you work out the number of neutrons?
faq.a: Take the mass number and subtract the atomic number. For sodium, 23 minus 11 gives 12 neutrons.
asks: How many neutrons does an atom have?

faq.q: How many electrons does an atom have?
faq.a: In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the atomic number. So carbon, atomic number 6, has 6 electrons.
asks: How do you find the number of electrons?

faq.q: Which number is which on the periodic table?
faq.a: The atomic number is always the smaller whole number. The mass number, or relative atomic mass, is the bigger one.
asks: Which number is the atomic number?

facts: Number of neutrons = mass number minus atomic number.
Sodium-23 has 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 11 electrons.
